I spoke with Dr. Amol Sadiwalla on the phone and explained my situation. He calmly told me not to worry and assured me that he would take care of everything. His confidence and kindness gave me a lot of trust and relief.

Soon after, my surgery was performed successfully. I am currently in the healing stage and recovering well. Whenever I visit for follow-ups, the doctor and the hospital staff treat me with great care and respect.

* Hospital facilities and patient care:

5 Stars for Dr. Ushma Patel
1 Star for Hospital Management & TPA

I recommend Dr. Ushma Patel. She has 25+ years of experience and it shows. She was incredibly kind, took the time to explain the entire laser ablation process for my Pilonidal Sinus, and even suggested cost-saving measures for my MRI (suggesting Cooper Hospital). If you are looking for a surgeon who actually listens and makes you feel at ease, she is the one.

The Hospital (STH Thunga, Andheri) Experience

While the medical care was fine, the operational side was a nightmare. Two major issues:

The "Trimmer" Disaster: I was admitted a night early for "prepping." I specifically requested a trimmer for the surgery site to avoid cuts and infection. The staff told me the "only trimmer in the ICU was broken/charging." They used a manual medical razor, which took 2+ hours and left me with several cuts in a very sensitive area. Tip: Bring your own trimmer here. They are clearly not equipped with basic working gear.

TPA & Insurance (The Raksha Plan Scam): I have a corporate MediBuddy plan with the "Raksha" benefit (express discharge). The hospital TPA completely ignored this. I was medically cleared to leave at 10 AM but wasn't allowed to step out until 4 PM. The coordination between the hospital TPA and the insurance team was non-existent.

The Refund Grind: I had to pay a 20k advance deposit. Despite being a cashless claim, it took 3 weeks of constant follow-ups with their accounts team to get my own money back.

Want to give a big shout out to Uma Budhaya for her promptness when i was seeking my old test reports. She immediately got into action when i mentioned i had missed collecting some of my previous reports and needed it since i was visiting my doctor. No unnecessary questions asked or made to feel i should have collected it before. She understood my situation, took my details and provided my reports immediately. Want to acknowledge her customer centicity and unconditional support.

On hearing this, the doctor became angry and said, “Whoever it is, I am not going to give any concession,” and abruptly hung up the phone. After that, the way my consultation was handled was extremely disappointing—something I could never have imagined. For a moment, I was even scared to ask him any questions.
I paid the full consultation fee as asked, and I had absolutely no issue paying it. However, the doctor should have at least clarified or spoken to me before reacting in such a manner.
I truly regret visiting based on my mother’s recommendation. I am a tax consultant by profession and have worked with reputed doctors in Mumbai. I have had direct professional interactions with well-known doctors from hospitals like SevenHills, Hinduja, and Surya Hospital, and I still have their direct contact numbers. Even today, if I have any concerns regarding my children or my husband, I can directly reach out to them. However, I have never had such a poor experience with any doctor before.
My mother continues to work there due to her financial condition, and she has no choice. I understand her situation. But after this experience, I will never visit this hospital again. This entire incident was extremely unprofessional and disappointing.

--------Thank you for responding to my review so quickly—I truly appreciate it.
I understand that my mother is an elderly woman, and she may sometimes ask for a discount. However, even if I had been charged ₹800 as a consultation fee, I would have paid it without any issue. My main concern was simply to get proper treatment for my skin infection. There was absolutely no need for such a reaction.
I would also like to mention that the hospitals I referred to earlier---------are places where I have known doctors personally since 2008. Till date, they have never charged me a consultation fee. So, this is not about the fee at all; it is about the way the situation was handled. The reaction was unnecessary and could have been avoided.
Honestly, I always pray to God that I have minimal need to visit doctors in life. During my consultation, when I asked Dr. Oswal whether I should use any normal anti-aging creams—as I am 40 years old and do not currently use anything on my skin—his response was quite unsatisfactory.

Anyway, I shared my experience as it happened. I sincerely hope that my mother receives respect at her workplace. Earlier, she worked at Dhanvantari Hospital, where everyone treated her very well. Yesterday’s experience, however, was quite different for me.

Thank you once again for your response. 🙏🙏🙏

Outside India currently and had my wife visit her clinic as she is currently pregnant. She had the most disturbing experience speaking with Dr. Vaishali Ghiya, the primary obstetrician at Carewel.

We had first visited Carewel 3 years ago for our first child. For the delivery, however, I had to take my wife to the hospital at 3 AM and there was no transport available. So we decided to go to the second hospital that we had registered in which was closer to where we live.

My wife had the Carewel file from her previous pregnancy which she carried  with her yesterday while visiting Carewel hospital. Dr Vaishali Ghiya was clearly upset that we chose to go to the second hospital on our list last time.

She made so many nasty comments that my wife almost cried. It's a shame that someone so educated has such a vile tongue. Some of the comments that she made are:

2. You should go to a government hospital

4. Why did you come here now? Why didn’t you go to the second hospital? Did something go wrong there?
5. Why are you coming when you are so far along?
6. There are two medicines, one for 1800, one for 2400 which one can you afford?

My wife and MIL, being kind and reserved, took these comments in silence. But is this any way for a doctor to talk to the patients? What kind of an example does it set for those working under her? Will nurses and wardboys also have the same attitude when a patient is admitted?

For perspective, my wife and I have a combined income of over 36LPA and, if we wanted, we could go to the most expensive hospital in Mumbai. We are shocked to see such an attitude from a doctor that treats women when they are at their most vulnerable. Honestly, I think we dodged a bullet here.
